name: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 12 (PPP2R2B)
aliases: autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia type SCA12

clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant ataxia caused by an expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the 5' region of PPP2R2B, which encodes a regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A; unusually the repeat lies outside the coding sequence rather than producing a polyglutamine tract
A characteristic early feature is a prominent postural and action tremor of the upper limbs that can be mistaken for essential tremor and may precede or overshadow gait ataxia
As the disorder advances patients develop cerebellar dysarthria, limb and gait ataxia, abnormal eye movements and hyperreflexia, with parkinsonian features or cognitive decline in some
Described in several populations but reported with particular frequency in certain Indian kindreds, so ancestry and a detailed family history can be useful clues
Brain MRI typically shows both cerebellar and cerebral cortical atrophy, reflecting the wider cortical involvement of this subtype
Diagnosis rests on sizing the CAG repeat within PPP2R2B; standard exome sequencing or panels that do not specifically assess this repeat will miss the diagnosis
No disease-modifying therapy exists, so care is supportive and multidisciplinary, with physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, gait aids and tremor management
reference.pathophysiology: SCA12 is caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the 5' regulatory region of PPP2R2B, which encodes the Bbeta regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A, a major serine/threonine phosphatase controlling neuronal signalling. Because the repeat lies outside the coding region, the mechanism is thought to be altered gene expression rather than a toxic polyglutamine protein, with dysregulated phosphatase activity disturbing neuronal signalling, calcium handling and survival. Purkinje cells and cerebral cortical neurons appear particularly vulnerable, producing the combination of tremor, progressive cerebellar ataxia and cortical features that characterises the disorder.
additionalDifferentials: Essential tremor, especially early when tremor dominates the picture
Repeat-expansion spinocerebellar ataxias (SCA1, 2, 3 and related types)
Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) in older men
Dystonic tremor and other combined tremor syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Targeted CAG repeat-sizing analysis of PPP2R2B to confirm the expansion
Brain MRI to document cerebellar and cerebral cortical atrophy and exclude structural causes
Testing for common repeat-expansion SCAs before or alongside PPP2R2B analysis
FMR1 premutation testing to exclude FXTAS in appropriate patients
Detailed three-generation family history to establish autosomal dominant transmission
Screening for acquired ataxia (thyroid function, vitamin B12, coeliac serology, alcohol history) and neuropsychological assessment where cognition is affected
redFlags: Rapid progression or an atypical course prompting reconsideration of an acquired, paraneoplastic or structural cause
Prominent early cognitive decline suggesting a broader neurodegenerative process
Dysphagia with recurrent aspiration requiring swallow assessment and airway protection
Recurrent falls with injury as gait ataxia worsens
reference.prognosis: SCA12 is slowly progressive over years to decades, with tremor and ataxia gradually becoming disabling and cognitive or parkinsonian features emerging in a subset. Life expectancy is often relatively preserved, and prognosis is influenced chiefly by falls, bulbar involvement and the degree of cortical dysfunction.
pitfalls: Labelling the patient with essential tremor and not pursuing a genetic cause when subtle cerebellar signs are present
Stopping investigation when common SCA panels are negative, thereby missing the PPP2R2B repeat
Relying on exome sequencing, which does not reliably detect this non-coding repeat expansion
Attributing the picture solely to Parkinson's disease when parkinsonian features appear
Failing to offer genetic counselling regarding dominant inheritance and variable expressivity
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Provide symptomatic and supportive care, as there is no disease-modifying therapy for the PPP2R2B expansion
Treat the prominent postural and action tremor symptomatically, trialling agents used for essential tremor such as beta-blockers or primidone
Maintain mobility and safety with physiotherapy, occupational therapy and gait aids, and offer speech and language therapy for dysarthria
Manage emerging parkinsonian features and cognitive decline with appropriate symptomatic treatment and neuropsychological support
Monitor progression with ataxia rating scales and surveil for falls and bulbar involvement
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance, with CAG-repeat sizing of PPP2R2B for at-risk relatives
